title: Fuzzy_agent
summary:
In computer science, a fuzzy agent is a software agent that implements fuzzy logic. This software entity interacts with its environment through an adaptive rule-base and can therefore be considered a type of intelligent agent.

Fuzzy logic is a form of many-valued logic in which the truth value of variables may be any real number between 0 and 1. It is employed to handle the concept of partial truth, where the truth value may range between completely true and completely false. The term fuzzy logic was introduced with the 1965 proposal of fuzzy set theory by mathematician Lotfi Zadeh. Fuzzy logic assigns a "degree of truth" between 0 and 1, and can therefore handle propositions that are vague and partially true.

Neural networks based artificial intelligence and fuzzy logic are, when analyzed, closely related. The underlying logic of neural networks is fuzzy. A neural network will take a variety of valued inputs, give them different weights in relation to each other, combine intermediate values a certain number of times, and arrive at a decision with a certain value. Fuzzy logic has been applied to many fields, from control theory to artificial intelligence, making fuzzy agents useful in domains where precise binary decisions are inadequate for handling real-world uncertainty and ambiguity.
